Flopped. Then classic.

Shawshank opened 32 years ago today and lost money. Hindi cinema has its own list:
1959 Kaagaz Ke Phool: India's first CinemaScope film and a box-office bomb. Guru Dutt never officially directed again.
1970 Mera Naam Joker: Raj Kapoor's four-hour epic. It failed; a shorter cut did well in the '80s.
1994 Andaz Apna Apna: flopped, and now everyone quotes it.
2004 Swades: a commercial disappointment that's now called one of Shah Rukh Khan's best.

Jim Henson would be 90 today.

Born 24 September 1936 in Greenville, Mississippi. He made his first puppet show, Sam and Friends, as a University of Maryland freshman in 1955, with a classmate named Jane Nebel. He married her four years later.
His actual invention was material: foam rubber and fabric instead of carved wood, because a hand bends and a wooden jaw doesn't.
Sesame Street from 1969. Fraggle Rock. The Dark Crystal. Labyrinth. He died in 1990, aged 53.

text:
24 September 1991. One Tuesday, three classics, same morning.

Nevermind — Nirvana. Made for $65,000. Geffen hoped for 250,000 copies. It entered the chart at 144, hit number one in January, and has sold over 30 million.
Blood Sugar Sex Magik — Red Hot Chili Peppers. Recorded in a reportedly haunted Los Angeles mansion. It gave them Under the Bridge and a career.
The Low End Theory — A Tribe Called Quest. Jazz bass, almost no clutter, Q-Tip and Phife trading verses.
Trompe le Monde — Pixies. Britain got it on the 23rd, America on the 24th. Their last album for 23 years.
And Soundgarden's Badmotorfinger was booked for the same day, until A&M pushed it to 8 October.

Which one still holds up?
